Buying Real Estate in Mexico as a Foreigner: A Simple Guide for Buyers in San Carlos, Sonora

Buying property in Mexico can feel confusing at first, especially if you’ve heard about restricted zones and trust structures. The good news is that the process is straightforward once you understand how it works, and thousands of foreigners purchase property safely every year. If you are looking at San Carlos, you’re in one of the most attractive and secure areas for foreign buyers. Sonora also offers the Only Sonora program, which allows free automotive transit for up to six consecutive months, making it even easier for U.S. and Canadian buyers to travel by car while owning a home here.

Why Foreigners Can Buy Property in Mexico

Foreigners are allowed to own property in Mexico, including beachfront property, through a structure called a fideicomiso, or trust. This applies to homes within the Restricted Zone (50 km from the coast and 100 km from international borders), which includes San Carlos. This system has been in place for decades and is widely used by international buyers.

What is a Fideicomiso?

A fideicomiso is a property trust created through a Mexican bank. Even though the bank technically holds the title, you are the sole beneficiary with full control. You can sell, remodel, rent out, pass the property to your heirs, or use it however you like. It functions very similarly to ownership. 
A fideicomiso is valid for 50 years and can be renewed indefinitely. The bank simply acts as a neutral trustee and has no say in how you use your property.

How the Buying Process Works

Connect with a Local Expert
Your first step is choosing a real estate agent who understands foreign transactions, fideicomisos, and local regulations. This guidance ensures your purchase is safe and compliant.

Discuss Payment Type
Foreign buyers have two ways to pay for a property: upfront payment or financing through a mortgage.

a) Paying upfront: You cannot pay the full amount in cash due to Mexico’s “Ley Antilavado,” which helps prevent money laundering. A bank deposit must be made when you sign the trust and deed at the notary. Some cash can be used, but only within legal limits. Paying upfront may also give you room to negotiate a better price and a faster closing. 

b) Financing through a mortgage: To qualify, you must be a temporary resident or hold another valid immigration status. You must provide proof of income from the U.S. along with a credit score report. Additional paperwork may be required, such as a criminal background check or a co-signer. Mortgages typically require 20% down, with the remainder financed over 15 to 20 years. Banorte is one of the banks that offers mortgage options for foreigners.

Make an Offer
Once you find the right property, your agent drafts a written offer that includes price, timelines, contingencies, and items included in the sale.

Open Escrow and Conduct Due Diligence
After the offer is accepted, funds are placed into a secure escrow account. Your agent and a notary begin verifying property documents, ownership records, and closing requirements.

Set Up the Trust (Fideicomiso)
Your agent coordinates with a bank to establish your property trust. The bank becomes the legal titleholder, while you remain the sole beneficiary with full rights over the property.

Sign and Close at the Notary
On closing day, you review and sign your fideicomiso agreement and deed with the notary. Once the documents are registered, the property is officially yours.

Costs Involved in the Process

While fees vary by region and property type, here are common closing costs:
• Appraisal (Avaluo)
• Trust Setup Fee (one-time)
• Annual Trust Fee
• Notary Fees
• Acquisition Tax (2–4% depending on municipality)
• Escrow Fees (promesa de compra-venta)
• Legal review or attorney fees (optional)
Your agent can estimate total costs before you make an offer.

Why San Carlos is a Great Choice for Foreign Buyers

San Carlos is known for its safety, U.S. and Canadian-friendly community, and beachside lifestyle. Sonora’s Only Sonora program also makes it easy for foreign homeowners to drive their vehicles into the state for up to six months without additional permits.

Sonora borders Arizona, and San Carlos is only about a 6-8 hour drive from cities like Tucson or Phoenix. The area offers clear processes, experienced professionals, and a stable environment for real estate investment.

How to Make Friends in San Carlos as a Newcomer

Moving to a new town can be exciting, but let’s be honest—it can also feel a little lonely at first. When we first arrived in San Carlos, I didn’t know anyone outside my family. But little by little, through everyday activities and casual interactions, I started meeting wonderful people who made me feel at home.

The good news is that San Carlos has one of the friendliest communities you can imagine. Locals and expats are welcoming, and because it’s a small town, it’s easy to start recognizing familiar faces in no time. Here are a few easy ways to make friends and connect with the community without too much effort.

Join the Local Gym

There is only one gym in town, and that makes it one of the best places to meet people. It’s called Athletic’s Club, and it offers a variety of activities, from yoga and zumba to water aerobics, spinning, and strength training.

What I love most about this gym is that people don’t just go to work out—they go to socialize. The classes are very community-oriented, and you’ll find both Spanish-speaking and English-speaking groups who are always happy to welcome newcomers.

Even if you’re not big into fitness, the group classes are worth trying just for the friendly atmosphere. It’s one of those easy, low-pressure ways to meet people organically while doing something good for yourself.

Try Pickleball or Padel

Pickleball and padel are huge in San Carlos right now. These sports have become very popular among both locals and expats, and the best part is that they’re naturally social.

Clubs often post their class schedules and tournament announcements on social media, so you can easily stay up to date. I usually repost local events and tournament updates on my own pages, so feel free to follow my social accounts if you want to stay in the loop.

Even if you’re a beginner, don’t be sh. Most players are welcoming and happy to teach new people. You’ll find yourself part of the local sports community before you know it.

Connect Through Church

If faith is part of your life, you’ll find several active church communities here in San Carlos. Most are Catholic, but there are also Christian and Mormon congregations, among others.

Church groups tend to organize family-oriented gatherings and events, which can be a wonderful way to connect with others who share your values. Even if you’re not a regular churchgoer, attending a community event can be a great opportunity to meet people and get involved.

Visit Coffee Shops and Local Restaurants

Some of the best conversations I’ve had in San Carlos started over brunch or coffee.

Cafes and restaurants are great spots to meet people, especially during brunch hours when the town feels most alive. At some point, you’ll probably find yourself exchanging smiles or small talk with the table next to you. If people start seeing you around regularly, they’ll usually strike up a conversation and welcome you to the area.

Coffee shops tend to attract digital nomads and remote workers, so if you work online, you might meet others doing the same (or racing for the wall sockets). Most cafes and restaurants offer free WiFi and a relaxed environment that makes it easy to connect naturally.

Get Out and Explore Town

Sometimes, the easiest way to meet people is simply by being out and about.

Take walks around the Marina at Marina Terra, visit El Mirador for the views, or stroll along the beachfront by the main boulevard. These are popular spots where locals walk their pets, enjoy the views, or just hang out.

You’ll notice that during the cooler months, especially in fall and winter, more people are outside enjoying the fresh air. A friendly smile or a simple “hello” often leads to casual conversations and even friendships.

Join Online Groups and Forums

San Carlos has an active online community that makes it easy to stay informed and meet people before even leaving the house.

Start by joining Facebook groups like “What’s Up San Carlos.” You’ll find event announcements, local recommendations, and sometimes even people organizing get-togethers.

There’s also a fun Spanish-English conversational group that meets at Colibrí’s Café. It’s a relaxed way to practice languages and make new friends at the same time.

Just browsing online or commenting on posts often leads to local connections—you’ll be surprised how fast you can become part of the conversation.

Final Thoughts

San Carlos might be small, but it’s full of opportunities to meet great people. Whether you prefer group activities, social sports, faith-based communities, or casual conversations over coffee, you’ll find your circle here.

What helped me the most was simply showing up—saying hello at the gym, joining a local class, or attending a small event. Before long, you start to feel like part of the community.

So if you’re new in town, get out there and explore a little. This town has a way of making newcomers feel right at home. Let us know if you have any questions,

The Best Grocery Shopping in San Carlos: How to Save Money and Eat Well

One of the biggest surprises for people moving to San Carlos, Sonora, is how convenient and affordable the grocery shopping experience is. Whether you are a full time resident or a snowbird visiting for the winter, you will find a great mix of local markets, big box retailers, and modern delivery services.

After living here for several months, I have perfected a routine that keeps my kitchen stocked with healthy food while keeping my budget in check. If you are wondering where to buy groceries in San Carlos and how to save the most money, here is my personal guide.

Walmart Online: Same Day Delivery to San Carlos

I handle the majority of my pantry shopping through Walmart Online. This is an absolute game changer for expat life in San Carlos because they deliver directly to your door, often on the same day you order.

I use this service for bulkier items and daily essentials. I typically buy my coffee, sweeteners, snacks, and shelf stable goods here. They also have an impressive selection of American canned goods like chili beans and Pillsbury dough, alongside specialty items for sugar free or diabetic friendly diets.

Beyond food, Walmart is my go to for cosmetics, beauty products, and basic household tools. While not every neighborhood in San Carlos is currently in the delivery zone, it is worth checking your address. If you are within range, it saves a significant amount of time and gas money.

Sam’s Club Guaymas: Bulk Savings on High Quality Proteins

When it comes to meat, dairy, and cleaning supplies, Sam’s Club in Guaymas is where I see the most significant savings. It is located right at the entrance of Guaymas Norte, making it a quick and easy drive from the heart of San Carlos.

Buying in volume allows me to portion my proteins at home and stretch my monthly budget. I highly recommend looking for these specific brands:

Rancho 17: A premium Sonora beef brand known for incredible quality.

Aires del Campo: My choice for free range and antibiotic free chicken.

Frozen Staples: I always grab Pilgrim’s Cordon Bleu chicken, buffalo wings, and waffles for quick meals.

The cheese selection at Sam’s Club is excellent for expats, featuring everything from sharp cheddar and mozzarella to convenient sandwich slices. If you have a large family or enjoy cooking from scratch, a Sam’s Club membership is a must for living in the San Carlos area.

Abarrey San Carlos: The Best Local Produce and Fresh Finds

For quick trips and fresh ingredients, Abarrey is my favorite local supermarket right in town. This is the best place to find high quality fruits and vegetables without leaving San Carlos.

The produce section at Abarrey is consistently top notch. In addition to fresh greens, they carry Rancho 17 beef, Kowi pork, and a variety of local seafood. There are a few unique features that make Abarrey special:

Fresh Orange Juice: They have an automatic machine that squeezes juice right in front of you.

Tortilla Variety: You can find both authentic homemade corn tortillas and commercial flour tortillas.

International Goods: They stock a surprising amount of American candies, frozen tamales, and pre made meals.

Abarrey is perfect for those spontaneous weekend cookouts or when you just need a few items for dinner. It combines the convenience of a neighborhood market with the selection of a much larger store.

Mastering Your San Carlos Grocery Routine

Grocery shopping in San Carlos is both simple and affordable once you know the local secrets. By balancing Walmart online deliveries for convenience, Sam’s Club for bulk savings, and Abarrey for fresh local finds, you can enjoy a high quality lifestyle without overspending.

If you are planning a move to San Carlos or just visiting for the season, you will find it easy to keep your pantry full of both local Mexican flavors and familiar international brands. Living in this beautiful coastal community is much easier when you have your shopping routine dialed in.

San Carlos Mexico Cost of Living: Monthly Budget for Digital Nomads

When researching a move to Mexico, San Carlos, Sonora often ranks as a top choice for digital nomads and families alike. This coastal town offers a unique blend of safety, scenic beauty, and affordability. It attracts a diverse community of Mexican families, retirees, and remote workers seeking a slower pace of life by the Sea of Cortez.

After living in Vancouver, Canada, and spending two years in our hometown, our family relocated to San Carlos. The transition highlighted a significant difference in both cost and quality of life. Our current expenses are roughly half to one third of our previous Canadian budget, allowing for a more balanced and enriched lifestyle.

The following breakdown outlines the monthly cost of living in San Carlos, Mexico, based on a family of four.

Monthly Cost of Living Breakdown

A typical monthly budget for a comfortable, family oriented lifestyle in San Carlos generally totals between 2,300 USD and 2,500 USD.

  • Housing (Rent or Mortgage): 800 USD to 1,000 USD

  • Groceries and Food: 800 USD to 1,000 USD

  • Utilities and Services: 300 USD

  • Gym and Kids Activities: 120 USD

  • Dining Out and Entertainment: 200 USD to 300 USD

  • Transportation: 150 USD

  • Private Bilingual School Tuition: Varies by institution

Housing Options in San Carlos

Selecting a neighborhood is a critical step when relocating to Sonora. Different areas cater to specific priorities such as proximity to bilingual schools, safety, or beach access.

We chose to live in Condominios Coral within the Ranchitos Campestre sector. This location is convenient for the Miramar Shortcut, which simplifies the school commute. Additionally, this area provides easy access to the only gym in town and reliable grocery delivery services from Walmart, which is not available in every neighborhood.

If you are exploring San Carlos real estate or rentals, consider these areas:

  1. Ranchitos Campestre: Offers affordable, family friendly homes with reliable utility connections.

  2. San Carlos Country Club: Ideal for those seeking a high end environment that remains reasonably priced.

  3. Coastal Zones: Best for those prioritizing direct ocean views and walking distance to the water.

Food and Grocery Expenses

One advantage of living in San Carlos is the accessibility of high quality food. For home cooking, Walmart offers same day delivery for proteins, vegetables, and pantry staples. For specialty items or international products, these local markets are highly recommended:

  • Santa Rosa Market: Located on the Main Boulevard near the Ranchitos and Country Club intersection. They stock imported Costco products and international goods.

  • Abarrey Supermarket: Found at the Marinaterra roundabout, known for fresh produce and fresh squeezed orange juice.

Dining out is also affordable. Many expats and retirees eat out daily, as restaurant meals typically range from 7 USD to 15 USD.

Utilities and Essential Services

While utilities are affordable, digital nomads should be aware of specific local conditions:

Internet Connectivity Telmex is the primary provider. While generally decent, outages can occur during storms. Many tech workers and remote employees in San Carlos are now opting for Starlink satellite internet to ensure a stable connection for work.

Water Quality The local water commission (CEA) provides water suitable for cleaning and showering. However, due to salinity and treatment processes, it is not recommended for drinking. Most long term residents install home water filtration systems or water softeners.

Electricity CFE provides reliable power, though short outages can happen during the summer storm season.

Transportation and Education

San Carlos is a compact town, but most residents own a vehicle due to limited public transportation. A monthly gas budget of approximately 150 USD allows for local errands and occasional trips to nearby Guaymas or Hermosillo.

For families, San Carlos offers several education paths. Our children attend a private bilingual school with a strong curriculum. Tuition varies significantly between local public schools and international private institutions, providing options for various budgets.

Is San Carlos Mexico Right for You

Relocating to San Carlos has provided our family with a higher quality of life and better work life balance. If you are considering a move to Mexico as a digital nomad or an expat family, the combination of warm weather and a welcoming community is hard to beat.
